portrait-davit-ruddock.webp.prompt:
A character portrait in a painterly fantasy-realism style, the classic CRPG portrait look: head and shoulders, three-quarter view, looking at the viewer, dramatic soft key light, a dark, softly painted background. No text, lettering, borders or frames.

Ironhull art direction: gritty industrial realism. Welded, rusted and patched metal, sodium-lamp orange against deep shadow, grime, steam and soot, everything built for work and mended rather than replaced.

Art bible for the Ostry system. Palette: burnt orange, rust brown, pale sky blue, deep sea blue, deep navy blue and oxblood. Lighting: A dim red sun that gives almost nothing. Real light comes from sodium lamps, orange and low, hung from cables and bolted to walls, with long shadows and hard pools of colour. Against the ice the lamps look warm and the shadows look blue. Gaunt's slate and sea-blue bulk throws a cold glow, and its lightning flickers across everything. Architecture: Towns cut down into the ice in terraces and shafts, with welded hab modules bolted into the walls like barnacles. Hab rings are clamped to rock and ice. Stations are stacked tanks, pipe-gantries and scoop arms. Everything is modular, extended in whatever shape the last repair allowed, with stairs added after the fact and walkways hung over drops. Materials: Rusted plate, weld seams, patched hull-steel, frost-furred pipe, sodium glass, coiled cable, ice-blue walls scored by cutters, and tarpaulin and sealant in mismatched colours. Everything is repaired, nothing is replaced, and everything wears a skin of frost or oil. Mood: Cold, close and watchful. The mood is warm company in a hard place, with a held breath behind it, as people keep half an eye on a lane they would rather not name. Design language: Ironhull: welded, modular, rusted and patched, sodium-lamp orange, hab rings bolted to rock. Here it shows as lamp-orange plate against sky-blue ice, with spare modules welded on and every surface carrying a repair someone is proud of.

Davit Ruddock, skimmer pilot, at Ostry Skim (Ostry Skim). A stocky man of about fifty with a sunburnt, lined face, thinning sandy hair and a hearing-aid clipped behind one ear. He wears a scorched orange flight-suit, lightning-burn marks on one sleeve, and a battered scoop-crew badge on his chest.

Who they are: He drops scoops into Gaunt's cloud tops for a living and has done it more times than he can count. He is calm, funny and a little deaf from the lightning. He is the one who tells new pilots which storms to leave alone.

Their people: Ostry is cold, and people here measure everything against that. They greet you by asking whether you have been fed, and they mean it. Credit is kept short and favours are kept long. Nobody says Varrow aloud if they can say 'the other side' instead, and nobody asks a Varrow family what it saw. Strangers are given a seat near the stove and a close look. Navy uniforms get the same politeness a dog gets from someone who has been bitten, and Blackhulls are 'cousins' or 'nobody I know'. People swear by the lamps, by the ice and by the tanks. Ostry pays more for food than anyone in the March, and complains about it with great skill.

The background is the dim bar of the port, out of focus, in the system's palette.
